archetypes.name: detection-scope-fit
archetypes.rationale: The reported bug is POSIX character classes in dynamic awk match() — entirely ASCII; the proposed lint targets non-ASCII bytes, leaving the root cause class undetected.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the issue description carefully: the root-cause CI failure was `[[:space:]]` inside a dynamic `match()` string argument — an ASCII-only POSIX character class that mawk does not support in string-mode regex. Then read the plan's Rule 1 and Rule 2 detection logic, which keys off non-ASCII byte presence. Determine whether an ASCII-only dynamic awk regex containing `[[:space:]]`, `[[:alpha:]]`, or similar POSIX bracket expressions — with no non-ASCII characters on the line — would be flagged by the proposed lint. Check whether the test fixtures include any ASCII-only POSIX character class case, or whether every Rule 2 fixture pairs the POSIX class with a non-ASCII character (em-dash) that does the actual triggering. Identify whether the plan proposes a companion detection rule for POSIX bracket expressions in dynamic string arguments, or explicitly scopes them out with a stated rationale. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stage-push-reachability
archetypes.rationale: The HEAD-non-advance check fires after `_stage_and_push_ci_fixes` returns 0, but when the vendor makes no changes, that function may return non-zero (nothing to stage), making the new detection branch unreachable.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read the `scripts/ship-pr.sh` plan section and locate the proposed insertion point: HEAD comparison fires after `_stage_and_push_ci_fixes` returns successfully (exit 0). Then read the current `_stage_and_push_ci_fixes` implementation to determine its behavior when the working tree and index are both clean — specifically whether it exits 0 (nothing to do) or exits non-zero (no staged changes means nothing committed). If it exits non-zero on an empty index, the `run_ci_fix_vendor` early-return at the existing `wrapper_rc` check fires before the new HEAD comparison code is reached, meaning the no-commit detection branch is dead code on the primary failure path. Also examine whether the `test-ship-pr.sh` regression case stubs `_stage_and_push_ci_fixes` (or `git-commit.sh`) to return 0 with no commit, or whether it relies on the real implementation — if the real implementation exits non-zero on an empty index, the stub must override it for the test to exercise the new branch. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
